text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is officially diagnosed when your readings are consistently at or above 130/80 mm Hg.
Blood pressure is measured with two numbers:

list.snippet: Systolic (top number): The pressure in your arteries when your heart beats.
Diastolic (bottom number): The pressure in your arteries when your heart rests between beats.

text_blocks.snippet: The American Heart Association and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention break down blood pressure into these ranges:

snippet_links.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

list.snippet: Elevated: Not yet high blood pressure, but a sign that you are at risk of developing it.
Stage 1 Hypertension: Doctors usually recommend lifestyle changes and may consider medication depending on your heart disease or stroke risk.
Stage 2 Hypertension: Typically requires a combination of medication and lifestyle adjustments.

Hypertensive Crisis (Above 180/120): Wait 5 minutes and test again. If it is still this high and you have symptoms like chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, or vision changes, call 911 immediately.
